data.reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed all package files and found no malicious injections. The PKGBUILD follows standard AUR practices, downloading from the official GitHub repository with a pinned tag and SHA-512 checksum. The qwen model's inconclusive verdict was solely due to transient API errors (HTTP 400) when attempting to review .SRCINFO and .nvchecker.toml, not due to any actual security concerns.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error in the qwen model (LLM API HTTP 400 BadRequestError), which prevented it from completing its review of .SRCINFO and .nvchecker.toml and forced an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model reviewed all files successfully and correctly identified the package as safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .SRCINFO and .nvchecker.toml due to API errors (HTTP 400)
learnings: Implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for transient LLM API errors (like HTTP 400/500) to prevent incomplete audits from skewing the final verdict.
When aggregating multiple model reports, distinguish between 'inconclusive due to security ambiguity' and 'inconclusive due to tool/API failure' to avoid unnecessary escalations.
